articles.title: Week 3 college football viewer's guide: It's LSU vs. Ole Miss, and then everything else
articles.summary: You might have heard that Lane Kiffin's LSU is playing at Ole Miss this weekend.
articles.body:
Hey, did you know that Lane Kiffin is returning to Ole Miss this weekend?

The biggest September game of the year is here after Kiffin's messy departure to LSU came as the Rebels were heading to the College Football Playoff.

Both LSU and Ole Miss are 2-0 and while the loser of Saturday night's game won't be eliminated from College Football Playoff contention by any means, a trip to the SEC title game will be a far smaller possibility.

Here are the games to watch in Week 3. And yes, there are actually other matchups between ranked opponents outside of the one in Oxford.

Oddly enough, these teams already have a common opponent. Houston beat Oregon State 33-20 in Week 1, while Texas Tech traveled to Corvallis in Week 2 and got a 35-24 win after outscoring the Beavers 14-3 in the fourth quarter. The winner will have a massive early advantage in the race to the Big 12 title game.

Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson threw for 413 yards against the Red Raiders as freshman receiver Jesse Legree had eight grabs for 240 yards and two scores. Just one opponent had more than 300 yards passing against the Red Raiders all season in 2025. And that came in Tech's loss to Arizona State .

If this is a much shakier pass defense, Houston QB Conner Weigman is a great candidate to exploit it. The former Texas A&M transfer threw for 305 yards and averaged 10 yards an attempt against the Beavers before throwing three TDs on just 12 passes in a Week 2 rout of Southern.

Texas Tech's Will Hammond is 46-of-60 passing for 487 yards so far this season, as former Boston College QB Thomas Castellanos saw playing time in sub-packages. Castellanos threw an 8-yard TD in his Tech debut against Oregon State and rushed five times for 15 yards and a score.

Perhaps no game is more suited for broad sweeping judgments than the Tar Heels ' visit to Clemson.

A win for North Carolina would be seen as exactly the type of victory Bill Belichick was hired to provide when he replaced Mack Brown. It'd also be a sign for many that the Week Zero victory UNC had over TCU was less of a fluke and more that the program is trending toward contender status in the ACC. The perception of a loss would also change based on how the game plays out. Close? Maybe North Carolina is a middling team. A blowout? Maybe Belichick will never get it done in Chapel Hill.

A Clemson loss would be further proof in a lot of fans' eyes that Dabo Swinney's empire is in a state of irreparable decline. A win? Well, these are the types of games Clemson should win.

OK, we're done with the hyperbole. Clemson is giving true freshman QB Tait Reynolds his first start after he saw playing time in each of the first two games. Reynolds was 16-of-27 passing for 178 yards in the Tigers' storm-delayed win over Georgia Southern in Week 2.

UNC easily took care of business against East Tennessee State and has allowed just 13 points through its first two games of the season.

If you're a strong believer that Miami, SMU and Louisville are the three best teams in the ACC, then this could end up as an elimination game for the ACC title.

SMU was incredibly sloppy in its 27-24 win over Florida State to cap Week 1. The Mustangs turned the ball over four times and missed a field goal yet needed a 20-yarder with 21 seconds to go to get the victory. Louisville lost 41-38 to Ole Miss in Week 1 as nine penalties helped prevent the Cardinals from capitalizing on two Ole Miss first-half turnovers.

Both teams waxed FCS opponents in Week 2. There wasn't much to learn from either of those wins. Louisville's ability to run the football could ultimately be the deciding factor. Florida State rushed for 199 yards against the Mustangs and Lincoln Kienholz gives coach Jeff Brohm a running threat from the quarterback position that he hadn't had in recent seasons.

The opponents have been Florida Atlantic and Campbell, but Gators fans have to love what they've seen from the Florida offense so far this season. Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo is 32-of-42 passing for 517 yards and five touchdowns, while Jadan Baugh has rushed for 296 yards and five scores on just 28 carries. Right behind him, CJ Hester has 42 carries for 271 yards and three scores.

Can that pace even remotely keep up against an Auburn defense that held Baylor to just 103 rushing yards on 45 carries?

It's also a chance for Auburn QB Byrum Brown to bounce back from a rough opener against the Bears. Brown, who came with coach Alex Golesh to Auburn, was 26-of-35 passing but threw three interceptions and rushed 21 times for just 27 yards and a score. He was much more productive on the ground against Southern Miss in Week 2 with 13 carries for 88 yards.

It's a bit of a shame the first SEC game between Golesh and new Florida coach Jon Sumrall is on at the same time as the game everyone has had circled on their calendars for months. The outcome is going to have a big effect on two fan bases desperate for a successful season.

What more can be said about this matchup? It's got about everything you could ask for from a college football game … and then some. The Oxford Police Department is getting assistance from from New Orleans and Mobile, Alabama, police as it boosts its gameday efforts. Oh, and LSU edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen was served with lawsuit papers at LSU's facility on Tuesday as part of Ole Miss' suit against him and Devin Harper following their January transfers to LSU.

Calling the atmosphere "hostile" in Oxford on Saturday night is an understatement, and don't be surprised if both teams are especially amped up early.

Could that lead to a Sam Leavitt interception or two? He's thrown four picks already this season and he surprisingly popped up as doubtful on LSU's injury report Wednesday with a reported sore shoulder.

Wisconsin transfer Dilin Jones has emerged as LSU's No. 1 back through the first two weeks of the season, but LSU also rushed for just 147 yards on 43 carries in Week 2.

Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy looked healthy after an injury scare in Week 1. After missing the end of the Rebels' win over Louisville in Week 1 with a thigh issue, Lacy had 13 carries for 87 yards and two scores against Charlotte in Week 2.

No. 5 Miami (-21) at Wake Forest (7:30 p.m. ET Friday, ESPN): The line doesn't reflect it, but there's always a chance of a Friday night home upset. Even if you don't think Miami has much of a chance of losing, it's still worth checking to see if QB Darian Mensah and WR Malachi Toney can continue their torrid start to the season.

Arizona State (-5.5) vs. Kansas (Noon ET, Fox Sports 1): The Big 12 opener for both teams is in London, as the conference is having the game at Wembley Stadium. Both teams are coming off big Week 2 losses, too. Kansas lost at home to rival Missouri by 17, and Arizona State fell apart in the second half against Texas A&M in a 48-20 defeat.

Florida State at No. 10 Alabama (-19.5) (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC): There doesn't seem to be much optimism at FSU that the Seminoles can repeat their Week 1 upset of the Crimson Tide from 2025. Alabama bounced back from a rough start at Kentucky in Week 2 for a 45-17 win. The Crimson Tide outscored the Wildcats 32-0 in the second half.

Mississippi State at South Carolina (-4) (4:15 p.m. ET, SEC Network): Kamario Taylor 's emergence at Mississippi State feels a bit like how LaNorris Sellers burst onto the scene at South Carolina. An upset win for the Bulldogs will be a sign that they could be this year's surprise team in the SEC.

Virginia Tech (-1.5) at Maryland (7:30 p.m. ET, FS1): Virginia Tech coach James Franklin and Maryland coach Mike Locksley were both assistants on Ralph Friedgen's Terrapins staff over two decades ago. Franklin was even once the coach in waiting at Maryland. Now, the winner will be halfway to bowl eligibility. In a make-or-break season for Locksley at Maryland, a win would be absolutely massive.

articles.title: LSU QB Sam Leavitt, initially 'doubtful' for high-profile matchup vs. Ole Miss, taken off injury report entirely
articles.summary: In just 2 days, Leavitt went from 'doubtful' to available ahead of Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford.
articles.body:
Looks like LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt will be available this weekend after all.

Ahead of Saturday's highly-anticipated matchup against Ole Miss , Leavitt is off the Tigers ' injury report, erasing a few days of uncertainty about whether he would be available to play against the Rebels.

In a surprise move, Leavitt was listed as "doubtful" on Wednesday , raising the possibility that No. 7 LSU would be taking on No. 8 Ole Miss without its starting QB. However, by Thursday, Leavitt was upgraded to questionable , with the quarterback reportedly participating in the team's walkthrough.

The report did not specify what injury was keeping Leavitt out; teams aren't required to list a reason or type of injury on SEC injury reports.

Leavitt, a redshirt junior transfer from Arizona State , has racked up 574 passing yards, two touchdowns, four interceptions and five rushing touchdowns across the first two games of the season.

Though multiple reports indicated that Leavitt had been limited in practice earlier this week, many were quickly skeptical of the injury designation. LSU head coach Lane Kiffin, known for these kinds of mind games , has high stakes entering the game: It will mark Kiffin's first return to Oxford since he left Ole Miss in December to take the Tigers job.

If the move was a gambit, it didn't seem to trick the Ole Miss coaching staff . In an appearance on the "Pat McAfee Show" on Friday, Rebels head coach Pete Golding relayed his initial response to a message from Kiffin about Leavitt being "doubtful."

"I got the text before the report went out from Lane, 'Hey, our quarterback's out,'" Golding said. "I'm like, 'Yeah buddy, I bet he is.' I've been around here a lot of Wednesdays with you, man, for 3 1/2 years, and I said I think our first one we had 42 guys on the first-ever SEC injury report on a Wednesday."

Any injury report shenanigans on Kiffin's part could result in him getting in trouble if they turned out to be inaccurate, with SEC rules stating that report releases "intended to hide a student-athlete's true participation status for competitive or strategic reasons" aren't allowed. Violation of that rule can result in a fine or punishment for the head coach.

articles.title: What makes Asian Games host Nagoya special? A city of cars, football, and sporting legacy
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: Best known as the home of one of the world’s biggest automobile manufacturers, Nagoya is a blend of industrial might, history and culture. Wha.
articles.body: NAGOYA: Best known as the home of one of the world’s biggest automobile manufacturers, Nagoya is a blend of industrial might, history and culture. What has largely flown under the radar, however, is the city’s rich sporting tradition, which goes beyond sumo wrestling, kendo or judo.As the Asian Games officially get under way here on Saturday, the Chunichi Dragons, formerly the Nagoya Baseball Club, are celebrating 90 years. Three years after the Dragons were formed, the Nagoya Grampus Eight football club was born.Now known as Nagoya Grampus, the club attracted international attention in the 1990s when it signed England great Gary Lineker and, later, Serbian star Dragan Stojkovic. Lineker spent two seasons in Nagoya before ending his playing career, while Stojkovic enjoyed seven stellar seasons at the club and remains an icon in the city.But the club’s football legacy was shaped just as significantly by a then little-known manager, Arsene Wenger.Wenger spent 18 months at Grampus before heading to Arsenal, where he would go on to become one of the most influential managers of his generation. At a testing stage of his managerial career, the Frenchman embraced the Japanese challenge and transformed Grampus from also-rans into Emperor’s Cup champions in 1995. Under Wenger, the club also won the Japanese Super Cup.For 65-year-old Toshio Kawakita, a lifelong Grampus supporter and now a volunteer at the Asian Games, the combination of Wenger and Stojkovic was the spark that helped reshape football in the city.“Wenger changed the way football was played here. He channelised our players’ passion for the sport and not just taught them tactics, he brought in a sense of purpose and direction. Stojkovic hugely helped Wenger in the process because he arrived here as a player first. Stojkovic returned to our club and under him we won the J League championship in 2010. We owe a lot of who we are as a club to them,” Kawakita said.Another Nagoya old-timer, Iori Tanaka, who runs a ramen shop near the Paloma Mizuho Sports Park, has his own memories of watching Lineker and Stojkovic in action.“Who would have thought that the Europeans would come and play football here? Both were at the fag end of their careers when they came here, but ensured a beginning of something new and lasting,” Tanaka said.Tanaka, though, could not resist a little cricket-related wishful thinking.“Who knows, if your cricketers (from India) play in the Japan Premier League, cricket too will get a huge boost here,” he said with a laugh.As the Asiad brings a generation of international stars to Nagoya, from Olympic champions and world medallists to Asia’s emerging sporting talent, the city is set to become a stage for some of the continent’s biggest names. For a city that has already played host to football greats such as Lineker and Stojkovic, and witnessed Wenger’s transformation of Japanese football, the Games offer a chance to make its sporting heritage part of a bigger story.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Darian Mensah, Malachi Toney's Box Score Stats, Highlights as QB Makes History in Miami's Win
articles.summary: Entering the day with a 91.1 completion percentage through his first two games, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah looked like he was going to improve that number on Friday by completing his first 24 passes in a 33-20 win over Wake Forest.
articles.body:
Entering the day with a 91.1 completion percentage through his first two games, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah looked like he was going to improve that number on Friday by completing his first 24 passes in a 33-20 win over Wake Forest.

Mensah did eventually throw four incompletions, finishing 30-of-34 for 220 yards. The Hurricanes, who entered the game favored by 20.5 points by FanDuel Sportsbook , got a tougher test from Wake Forest than expected.

Dating back to his final 11 completions last week, the junior quarterback completed 35 consecutive passes before his first off-target throw in the third quarter. He also threw three touchdowns to raise his season total up to 11 without an interception.

Malachi Toney was on the receiving end of 12 passes from Mensah. The Hurricanes star wideout put up 114 yards and third-quarter touchdown.

Mensah's 35 straight completions marks the second-longest streak in FBS history, but he did set new Miami and ACC records.

Elija Lofton and Joshua Moore were also on the receiving end of touchdown passes from Mensah.

The Heisman hype, despite still only being mid-September, was reaching a fever pitch for Mensah when it looked like Miami was going to cruise to an easy win.

The four incompletions for Mensah on Friday matched his total from the previous two games combined, but he is still completing close to 90 percent of his attempts overall (71-of-79).

One thing that might be of concern to Miami going forward is it needed Mensah and Toney to play as well as they did because the Hurricanes struggled to put away Wake Forest.

After trailing 31-7 midway through the third quarter, Wake Forest got touchdowns on back-to-back possessions that cut the deficit to 11. The Demon Deacons gave two points back with a safety on a holding penalty in their own end zone.

Wake's defense forced a three-and-out on Miami's next possession, then drove 64 yards to get deep in opposing territory. The Hurricanes defense finally got a stop on Gio Lopez's incomplete pass into the end zone on fourth-and-5 with 8:51 remaining to halt the run.

Even when the Hurricanes had opportunities to at least burn clock, their offense stagnated. They had a four-possession sequence that ended with three three-and-outs and a 54-yard field-goal attempt that was blocked to keep Wake Forest in it.

Lopez's interception to Ethan O'Connor with just over two minutes remaining allowed Miami to hold on for the win.

The second-half bumpiness, which saw the offense gain just 77 yards and pick up five first downs, took some shine away from what looked like another standout effort by Miami's dynamic duo early in the game.

Mensah and Toney remain close to unstoppable, but this game could be an indication they will need to keep playing near-perfect football for the Hurricanes to reach their ceiling this season.

One thing working in Miami's favor is the schedule is light until a Nov. 7 matchup with Notre Dame. Next week will see the Hurricanes return home to host Central Michigan before resuming ACC play against Clemson on Oct. 3.

articles.title: No. 13 Texas Tech escapes with 28-26 win over No. 22 Houston when Cougars' 2-point conversion try fails
articles.summary: Will Hammond is still the Red Raiders' starting QB job, leading Texas Tech to a win after Thomas Castellanos threw an interception on his first play.
articles.body:
No. 13 Texas Tech escaped an upset by No. 22 Houston with a 28-26 win in its Big 12 opener at Lubbock, Texas on Friday night.

Cougars quarterback Conner Weigman hit tight end Patrick Overmyer over the middle for a 10-yard touchdown with 49 seconds remaining in regulation. Needing a 2-point conversion to tie the score, Weigman attempted a run around left end but was tackled just short of the goal line.

The play was reviewed, but Weigman's knee appeared to be down before he stretched the football across the line. Replay officials upheld the call on the field, ruling there was not enough evidence to overturn the play.

J'Koby Williams' 29-yard touchdown in the third quarter put the Red Raiders ahead, 21-17, finishing a comeback from an inept start and early 10-point deficit on their home field at Galaxy Stadium.

The Cougars cut the deficit to 21-20 on a Jonathan Dimas field goal, but Texas Tech landed the decisive blow with an 87-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter that took 11 plays and ran six minutes off the clock.

Cameron Dickey finished off the long series with a 1-yard scoring run and a Stone Harrington extra point put the Red Raiders ahead, 28-20. And with that, he also extended Texas Tech's record to 12-0 when he gets a TD.

Houston began the game with a field goal on its first possession, but Texas Tech gave the ball right back. On Tech's opening play, QB Thomas Castellanos was chased from the pocket, rolled out to his right and floated a pass down the sideline that he was presumably trying to throw out of bounds. Instead, it was picked off by Will James.

Castellanos got the start on Friday, though head coach Joey McGuire confirmed that Will Hammond remains the starting QB and the team had scripted a couple plays for Castellanos at the beginning of the game.

Castellanos, a transfer from Florida State, signed with Tech in late August and he's appeared in a handful of plays in every game so far, throwing for a touchdown and running for two more, including one Friday.

Following the turnover, the Cougars went 55 yards in 10 plays for their first touchdown. Weigman finished off the drive with a pass over the middle to Amare Thomas, who stretched over the goal line for an 11-yard score.

Down 10-0 and running just one play after Castellanos' interception, Texas Tech turned back to Hammond in at quarterback. The Red Raiders subsequently went three-and-out with Hammond throwing two incompletions.

However, after its defense forced a punt, Texas Tech got back into the game with a 75-yard touchdown drive. Hammond hit Kenny Johnson for a 28-yard gain on a third-and-12. Then, four plays later, he connected with Johnson again for 35 yards down the right sideline and into the end zone.

Houston regained the lead at 17-14 before halftime on a 46-yard pass from Weigman to Koby Young, who made a spectacular catch for the touchdown.

Young trapped the ball and cradled it in his right arm before securing it with his right hand as he fell just inside the pylon.

Weigman finished with 282 yards and 3 TDs, completing 27 of 38 passes with no interceptions. On the Cougars' final touchdown drive, he completed all six of his throws.

Overmyer grabbed 8 receptions for 72 yards and a TD, while Amare Thomas caught 7 passes for 75 yards and a score. Makhi Hughes rushed for 71 yards on 15 carries, while Weigman added 56 on the ground with 13 attempts. Houston drops to 2-1 with the defeat.

For Texas Tech (3-0), Hammond completed 17 of 27 passes for 257 yards, 1 TD and 1 INT. Kenny Johnson caught 4 of his passes for 113 yards and a score. Castellanos ran for a TD on a direct snap near the goal line in the second quarter.

Dickey rushed for 65 yards and a TD on 16 carries, while Williams joined him in the end zone and tallied 62 yards on 7 rushes.

images.caption: Despite not starting the game, QB Will Hammond played most of the way and led his team to a win on Friday. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) (John E. Moore III via Getty Images)

articles.title: Aston Villa: Villa and Tottenham face crucial early season showdown
articles.summary: Aston Villa and Tottenham are winless in the Premier League - and both in need of inspiration as they prepare to face each other on Saturday.
articles.body:
More than half a billion spent between them, for just three points and one goal. Tottenham and Aston Villa are in need of Premier League inspiration.

It is not a surprise that a summer of change at both clubs has failed to bring immediate results - but they need to ignite their season.

They meet at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday as the past two Europa League winners but sitting in the bottom four of the early Premier League table.

With 10 new players, and six key sales - including Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins - Unai Emery is shaping a new Villa team.

Tottenham also added 10 players for more than £300m but goodwill is in short supply after two years of relegation battles. Victory is paramount for both teams.

At VIlla, Emery has credit in the bank after turning them from a team floundering in mid-table to Europa League winners - qualifying for Europe every season since his arrival, and getting them back into the Champions League this year.

This term there is a different remit, to be successful while integrating 10 new players - having spent more than £250m - following the summer exits.

Emery conceded he did not know exactly why Villa lost control during last Saturday's defeat by Nottingham Forest - but knows he was unable to make a significant impact from the touchline with all the new players still fitting in to their new set-up.

He can look frantic in his technical area during games, but has an impressive ability to decompress immediately and speak to the players calmly by the time he has returned to the dressing room.

Emery remains confident Villa will improve yet is relying on John McGinn and Tyrone Mings, as two of the senior players, to help him and the squad through a difficult patch.

It is a reason why both played in Wednesday's Carabao Cup win at Coventry rather than being rested.

Captain McGinn has previously described learning Emery's methods as doing "a lot of homework". That may be why Aaron Wan-Bissaka has struggled in his opening three games as he tries to adapt quickly - the same too for other new signings perhaps overthinking their roles.

An extended three-week break follows Saturday's match. But the head coach will not get the much-needed time on the training ground with his squad, as many go on international duty.

"This break is crazy because it's three weeks," Emery said. "I don't like to be three weeks but we must accept it.

"We are not going to have the players we want. [Johan] Manzambi played the first two matches with us and Saturday the third and then he goes with the national team.

"Back with us, we must again try to join him with us in our structure and his mind will maybe be confused.

"We don't want to use the international break as an excuse.

"Saturday is very important as we lack points but we continue in our process trying to work as well as possible."

Manzambi, brought in from Freiburg, and £47m winger Ibrahim Mbaye, who has moved from Paris St-Germain. made their debuts last weekend, coming off the bench against Forest, and are set to form part of a new attack.

Nicolas Jackson, signed from Chelsea in August, will start on Saturday after coming off the bench at the CBS Arena as Emery gets close to his preferred line-up, with Villa looking to click after notching just one point in their opening four games.

Only Villa, with 3.39, have a worse xG in the Premier League so far this season than Spurs' 3.45. Alysson's header in the 2-1 defeat by Forest was their first goal in the Premier League this term, with Spurs still searching for theirs.

Both are still worse than bottom club Coventry, who are pointless and goalless, but have an xG of 4.21.

Villa have had the lowest number of shots in the Premier League with 33, compared to Tottenham 's 51, while their six on target is also the worst in the top flight followed by Spurs' 12.

Only Hull have had fewer touches in the box (47) than Villa's 62.

Yet Villa's defence must still be wary of struggling Spurs despite the hosts' lack of goals.

Matty Cash is available after recovering from a muscle problem but fellow defenders Pau Torres and Ian Maatsen are out for a match in which Villa can expect to face pressure. Only Manchester United , Arsenal , Brighton and Liverpool have made more passes in the final third than Tottenham (617), who have the highest successful pass completion rate, at 81.4%.

Villa's tally of 32 crosses, the lowest in the league, is half as many as Tottenham have managed.

It has been 407 minutes since Spurs last scored in the Premier League. They have failed to score in four successive Premier League matches - the first time that has happened since September 2006.

Their stalemate with Everton was their first goalless draw at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the Premier League after 140 games.

But despite both sides' struggle for goals, history does not point to a 0-0 draw. None of the past 22 Premier League meetings between Spurs (15 wins) and Aston Villa (seven) have been drawn.

As Villa rebuild, they might hope a match against opponents struggling for wins might be the chance to kick-start their season. But they cannot afford to be lulled into a false sense of security.

articles.title: Real Madrid-Santiago Wanderers: La Fábrica busca el sello de calidad definitivo y el Bernabéu, otro hito
articles.standfirst: Hoy se juega en el coliseo blanco la Copa Intercontinental sub 20 (12.30 horas, RMTV), con una asistencia que podría superar el récord del Maracaná de 45.656 aficionados
articles.summary: Hoy se juega en el coliseo blanco la Copa Intercontinental sub 20 (12.30 horas, RMTV), con una asistencia que podría superar el récord del Maracaná de 45.656 aficionados
articles.body: Un título mundial juvenil para cerrar el círculo. Es lo que busca hoy el Real Madrid para encumbrar a su cantera, que lleva meses en boca de todos tras ganar la Youth League y tener un impacto histórico en el último mercado veraniego, generando al club unos ingresos de 210 millones de euros. La Fábrica busca el sello de calidad definitivo con la Copa Intercontinental sub 20, el único título que falta en las vitrinas de Valdebebas en el fútbol de formación. Una 'finalísima' que disputa hoy en el Bernabéu (12.30 horas, RMTV) ante el Santiago Wanderers chileno. El campeón de la Youth League contra el de la Libertadores sub 20. Un duelo por todo lo alto con el trono mundial en juego. El Madrid se vestirá de gala para la ocasión y para ello ha reunido a una selección de sus mejores 'joyas' (nacidos desde el 1 de enero de 2006). Tras aplazar los partidos de sus tres primeros filiales (Castilla, Madrid C y Juvenil A), a la 'galaxia juvenil' madridista sólo le faltará Thiago Pitarch, reclutado por el primer equipo. El resto de los disponibles estarán a las órdenes de Álvaro López, técnico del Juvenil A y artífice del título de la Youth que ha llevado al Madrid hasta la Intercontinental. Álvaro López tendrá a sus órdenes a 10 jugadores en plantilla del Castilla, 7 del Real Madrid C y 6 del Juvenil A, aunque varios de ellos en dinámica de los dos primeros filiales. En total, 23 jugadores, 20 de ellos campeones de la Youth League la pasada temporadas. De la lista destaca Sergio Martínez, el último fichaje del Madrid procedente del Racing, que se apunta a la gran cita tras debutar con el Castilla hace dos semanas. Junto a él, otros canteranos estelares como Javi Navarro, Joan Martínez, Mario Rivas, Cestero, Aguado, Yáñez, Roberto Martín, Carlos Díez o Ciria serán las grandes atracciones madridistas. Al partido no le faltará de nada para darle a la cita la importancia que se pretende. Florentino Pérez lo presidirá en el palco, habrá VAR, también control antidoping postpartido y el club ha solicitado su presencia a la grada de animación del Real Madrid para dar colorido y ambiente. Incluso, ayer a mediodía se organizó una visita al Bernabéu de ambos equipos para identificarse con el escenario. En el Madrid, sólo Cestero, Yáñez y Aguado han jugado en él. Otros pocos han estado en el banquillo, pero no han tenido minutos. “Es un sueño jugar en el Bernabéu porque crecemos viendo a nuestros ídolos jugando en ese campo. Que juguemos allí significa muchísimo para nosotros. Tenemos muchísimas ganas y vamos a dejarnos todo. El míster solo nos ha pedido que seamos nosotros mismos, que hagamos todo lo que llevamos haciendo hasta ahora", afirma el delantero madridista Yeremaiah, uno de los que se estrenará en el Bernabéu. El Real Madrid buscará un doblete inolvidable con motivo de esta Copa Intercontinental. No sólo busca el título, también una asistencia histórica en un Bernabéu que se espera supere los 40.000 espectadores. El Madrid se ha movilizado para hacer posible un récord de asistencia y las expectativas son muy altas. Socios gratis, máxima difusión, precios populares, invitaciones a la cantera... Todo para llenar lo más posible el coliseo madridista. La del Bernabéu será la quinta edición de la Copa Intercontinental sub 20, todas ellas celebradas en míticos estadios y con una asistencia espectacular tratándose de partidos de juveniles. Tal y como destaca UEFA.com, en la primera finalísima de 2022 el Benfica se impuso por 1-0 ﻿al Peñarol uruguayo en el Estadio Centenario de Montevideo ante 40.579 aficionados. Un año después, Boca Juniors se alzó con el trofeo contra el AZ Alkmaar con 37.386 personas en La Bombonera. En 2024, fue el turno del Maracaná, donde el Flamengo venció a Olympiacos ante 31.237 espectadores. articles.title: Carlos Soler vuelve a Mestalla 212 domingos después
articles.standfirst: El jugador de la Real regresa a Valencia como rival tras disputar su último partido como blanquinegro en agosto de 2022
articles.summary: El jugador de la Real regresa a Valencia como rival tras disputar su último partido como blanquinegro en agosto de 2022
articles.body: Carlos Soler pisó Mestalla por última vez el lunes 29 de agosto de 2022. Había llevado el brazalete de capitán en el partido contra el Atlético (con victoria rojiblanca 0-1). Estaba apurando sus últimas horas como jugador del Valencia, de forma totalmente consciente, un día antes de volar a París, para firmar para el PSG. Desde entonces, no había regresado al estadio del Valencia. Han pasado más de cuatro años, 1.483 días, 212 domingos. Hasta este fin de semana, con la camiseta de la Real Sociedad, a las 21:00 horas. "Vuelvo a casa, no lo había hecho desde que salí de allí. Para mí jugar en Mestalla es muy importante", dijo el futbolista txuri urdin esta semana en San Sebastián. Soler se fue traspasado al poderoso equipo francés por 18 millones de euros. Después pasó por el West Ham hasta que la temporada pasada fichó por la Real Sociedad. Precisamente, el equipo con el que ha vuelto a sentirse jugador importante -ganó la Copa del Rey la temporada pasada- fue el rival ante el que debutó en Primera división. Fue el 10 de diciembre de 2016, en Anoeta, con Cesare Prandelli en el banquillo y derrota por 3-2. Soler desprende una mezcla de respeto y cautela que resume su relación actual con el valencianismo: "Estoy con ganas de estar allí, de disfrutar de mi familia y amigos, de volver a la que siempre es mi casa. Vi su partido del lunes". El centrocampista de la Real ingresó en la cantera del Valencia en 2005 cuando entró en la Academia con 7 años recién cumplidos y allí fue quemando etapas sin miedo a ser identificado como una promesa clara en todas las categorías. Fue Voro el que, en una situación muy complicada, le dio galones titular. Y Marcelino, entre 2017 y 2019 lo convirtió en una pieza clave del proyecto de Champions que voló por los aires antes de la pandemia. El verano de 2022 iba a ser el de su renovación. No lo fue: las negociaciones no prosperaron y la posibilidad de una venta empezó a tomar forma. El 29 de agosto jugó su último partido como valencianista —con Gennaro Gattuso en el banquillo— y dos días después, el 31 de agosto, el Valencia oficializó su traspaso al PSG por 18 millones de euros más variables. Se iba tras 226 partidos, 36 goles, 31 asistencias y una Copa del Rey. Soler nunca escondió sus razones: "Decidí buscar jugar con los mejores en el PSG, jugar la Champions, intentar crecer a nivel deportivo y ya está". Pero la marcha de un capitán y canterano en ese momento tan concreto del club dejó una herida que tardó en cerrar. También lo reconocía después en otra entrevista: "Viéndolo desde fuera y poniéndome en su piel, sin saber todo lo que pudiera haber detrás, entiendo que los aficionados se enfadaran". Lo que vino después, sin embargo, no fue únicamente rechazo o despecho. "La gran mayoría, cuando voy por Valencia, me dicen: 'Ojalá vuelvas', 'qué pena que te fuiste'", cuenta Soler, que también relativiza el ruido más hostil: "Son muy pocos los que me insultan o insultan a mi familia". En la penúltima jornada de la temporada pasada, Carlos Soler se enfrentó por primera vez al Valencia, pero lo hizo en Anoeta. Este domingo pisará el césped del viejo Mestalla por última vez, pero con una camiseta distinta a la del Valencia. Hay pocas dudas de que la grada sabrá corresponder la actitud que tuvo el futbolista durante sus años en el club. Después de cuatro años, hay cosas que no se olvidan. Salvo cuando la pelota empiece a rodar. "Al Valencia le deseo lo mejor, menos este domingo".

articles.title: Algo se ha roto con la camiseta de Ceuta
articles.summary: 'Comprimidos', por Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.body: No comparto tu opinión pero defenderé siempre tu derecho a expresarla". Estoy muy de acuerdo con Voltaire y lo aplico al caso de las camisetas de Ceuta. No me pareció bien que Mbappé, Vinicius y Konaté hicieran ese feo con la camiseta. Pero por lo que sea no quisieron lucirlas (entre otras cosas porque nadie te puede obligar a mostrar ningún tipo de lema) y están en su absoluto derecho de actuar como lo hicieron. Eso sí, creo que algo se ha roto en cuanto a la relación del madridismo (no digamos ya las aficiones rivales) con estos tres jugadores. He percibido mucha decepción, mucho desencanto, mucha indignación con ellos. Y he leído ataques feroces durante toda la semana. Desgraciadamente, habrá un antes y un después de la camiseta. § Otra de matar al mensajero. A Jürgen Klopp le parece “patético” que los periodistas alemanes desvelasen su lista de convocados antes que él. Lo patético es culpar a la Prensa. § Simeone y Mou, frente a frente en un derbi 13 años después. El ánimo de revancha está del lado del portugués, ya que en su último enfrentamiento perdió en el Bernabéu. Era la final de Copa. § Aquel día, el vestuario del Madrid estaba hecho añicos. Mañana llega Mourinho con otro talante y bastante satisfecho del buen ambiente que ahora reina entre sus jugadores. § Muy positivo ver caras nuevas en La Roja. Muchas selecciones están obligadas a hacer una revolución: España, no. Pero sí es importante hacer una evolución. Conviene siempre mirar hacia el futuro y no anclarse en el pasado, por brillante y exitoso que haya sido. § Alguien me puede explicar cómo hemos llegado a esto de rogar ‘deme usted un Balón de Oro, por favor’. § ¿Y el Balón de Oro para el belga De Ketelaere? Fue el único futbolista que logró la proeza de marcarle un gol a España en el Mundial. Se lo merece. § Parece que OpenAI robó millones de artículos a The New York Times. Si lo que pretenden es matar el periodismo y a los Medios lo están logrando. Si no, también. § Leo de un tirón ‘A corazón abierto’, de Isaac Blázquez. Un valiente, honesto, descarnado y terapéutico texto en el que relata su recorrido por las calles más oscuras de la vida, sus idas y venidas, sus angustias, sus tormentas internas, su búsqueda de anhelada paz interior... Blázquez, más atlético que el oso del escudo, emociona con su mirada lúcida y sincera, con sus reflexiones certeras e inapelables. Spoiler: al final siempre sale el sol.

articles.title: Agoumé: "El 4-1 fue una tarde muy feliz para todos"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista atiende a MARCA en la previa de la visita del Barcelona al Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.summary: El centrocampista atiende a MARCA en la previa de la visita del Barcelona al Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.body: Hablamos con el sevillista Lucien Agoumé (Yaundé, Camerún, 2002) en la previa de la visita del Barcelona este sábado al Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. El centrocampista afronta su cuarto curso en Nervión y se ha convertido en el motor del equipo de Luis García Plaza. Desde Arabia Saudí le tentaron este verano, pero el ‘6’ quiere seguir creciendo como futbolista con la camiseta blanquirroja. Pregunta. Nueva jornada, poco descanso, pero se trabaja mejor después de una victoria. Respuesta. Sí, estamos muy contentos. Tocaba recuperarse bien para un partido donde habrá que correr mucho. Necesitamos energía, pero ya estamos enfocados. P. El equipo transmite seguridad y los números acompañan. ¿Qué ha cambiado? R. El año pasado no estábamos nerviosos durante los partidos, pero en el fútbol a veces no te salen bien las cosas. Este año estamos compitiendo bien, luchando como grupo y sumamos puntos, que es lo importante. Siempre falta algo porque somos un equipo joven y tenemos un margen de mejora grande como grupo y sobre todo tenemos muchos jugadores jóvenes que pueden hacerlo individualmente. Estamos todos de acuerdo. P. La afición se ha volcado con el equipo. En la arenga que dio antes del partido ante el Valencia habló de familia. R. Nuestra afición nos está apoyando mucho, los escuchamos todo el partido y espero que sigamos así. Este sábado creo que será espectacular y por qué no soñar. La unión es muy importante porque sabemos de dónde venimos y con esa unión, la entrega y el compromiso de todos, estamos trabajando bien. Esta palabra nos tiene que acompañar hasta el final. P. Llega el último partido antes del parón ante un equipo que asusta. R. El Barcelona lleva dos o tres años así. Ha empezado la temporada muy bien, pero es un partido de fútbol y nunca se sabe. No puedes ir a un partido pensando en perderlo. Lo hemos preparado de la mejor manera posible para hacerles daño. Está en un momento de forma brutal, pero es un partido de fútbol y cuando un partido empieza siempre pone 0-0. Vamos a salir con nuestra gente para intentar hacer el mejor encuentro posible. Lo hicimos el año pasado y ganamos. Intentaremos dejar la mejor versión del Sevilla. Pregunta. ¿Qué recuerda del 4-1? R. Recuerdo la euforia al final, cuando pita el árbitro, con la afición, con los compañeros, con toda la gente que trabaja en el club. Fue una tarde muy feliz para todos nosotros. Porque siempre hay que soñar y tener esa fe que trabajando, luchando, se pueden conseguir cosas. P. Si pudiera descartar a un jugador... R. Cualquier jugador del Barcelona te debe preocupar, hasta los del banquillo. Juegue quien juegue, el Barcelona siempre tiene la misma filosofía y los jugadores lo demuestran cada fin de semana. Han metido siete goles en el último partido, no será fácil pero nos hemos preparado y a ver lo que pasa. P. ¿Es el mejor momento de Agoumé desde que llegó al Sevilla? R. Eso no lo sé. Intento siempre dejar mi mejor versión en cada partido y si estoy o no en mi mejor momento, no lo puedo decir yo. Lo dice la gente que ve los partidos y si la gente está contenta, voy a seguir así sobre todo para ayudar a mis compañeros. Espero que sigamos sumando puntos y con ese momento de forma que tenemos ahora. Llevamos dos o tres años muy complicados y nos toca ahora un poco de felicidad. P. ¿En qué debe mejorar? R. En muchas cosas. La gente a veces me ve y parece que soy mayor, pero solo tengo 24 años y con esa edad hay muchas cosas que un futbolista y un hombre puede mejorar. Lo estoy trabajando todos los días en la ciudad deportiva con el cuerpo técnico, el míster y está dando sus frutos en el campo. Pregunta. La competencia ha subido con la llegada de un jugador como Fofana. Va a aprender mucho con él. R. Youssouf, Kocho, son dos jugadores de muy buen nivel y nos van a ayudar mucho. Fofana es internacional con Francia, no es fácil. Ha jugado en equipos como Mónaco y Milan, y todos sabemos sus cualidades. Nos va a aportar mucho dentro y fuera del campo con su experiencia. P. El Barcelona siempre ha seguido el mercado de las jóvenes promesas francesas. Usted estaba en su lista. R. Sí, pero son cosas de cuando era más chiquitito. Hubo algunos contactos pero hace mucho tiempo ya, era muy joven y nunca se concretó. El Barça es un equipo, un club enorme y muchas veces los jugadores jóvenes cuentan con el interés de varios clubes, pero se quedó ahí. P. Este verano parece que llegó una oferta, pero desde Arabia. R. Eso tendréis que preguntarle al club, yo no recibo las ofertas, (risas), pero no quería salir del Sevilla este verano. Me estoy encontrando muy feliz aquí, mi familia también en la ciudad, el club... Quiero seguir creciendo como jugador en este equipo, puedo mejorar muchas cosas y ser un mejor futbolista. Y lo quiero hacer en el Sevilla. Espero conseguirlo.

articles.title: Simeone-Mou, uno de esos duelos imprescindibles
articles.standfirst: Sus choques, 12 años sin ellos, son necesarios para una Liga algo devaluada
articles.summary: Sus choques, 12 años sin ellos, son necesarios para una Liga algo devaluada
articles.body: Más de 12 años han pasado desde la última vez que se midieron Simeone y Mourinho. Más de una década sin que dos de los técnicos más brillantes de este siglo, no es una exageración, crucen un abrazo previo, alguna indirecta en sala de prensa y, a buen seguro, una táctica más que estudiada. En eso son de los mejores, igual que en plantear campos de minas para los rivales. Entonces, El Cholo era el adalid de un equipo tan rocoso que se cargó (siendo inferior) al Real Madrid en una final de Copa del Bernabéu o al Chelsea en el mismísimo Stamford Bridge tras un 0-0 en el añorado Vicente Calderón. Poco queda del colmillo que tenía el luso, poco queda también de aquel Atlético defensivo e intenso. Ahora ambos presentan un nuevo rostro, por mucho que se empeñen los de siempre en tildar al Cholo de ultradefensivo. O no ven sus partidos o no tienen ganas de darle mérito alguno. En cualquier caso, el respeto entre ambos se mostrará hoy en sala de prensa y mañana sobre el verde de un estadio Metropolitano que verá el mejor derbi del planeta. Sí, no hay otro como un Atlético-Madrid en el mundo. Acabó la jornada entre semana con palos a José Alberto por salir con los suplentes del Racing. Parece mentira que no se sepa que su Liga es otra. Como la de Osasuna. Igual la reflexión debería ir a los motivos por los que los tres grandes ganan sobrados la mayoría de sus partidos en casa.

articles.title: Ethan Mbappé se gana el perdón de Davide Ancelotti... y una noticia muy especial: “Fue una semana muy importante para su crecimiento”
articles.standfirst: El hermano de Kylian se reivindicó marcando en el triunfo del Lille ante el Troyes tras ser expulsado contra el Betis en Champions · Recibió su primera convocatoria con la Sub21 de Francia
articles.summary: El hermano de Kylian se reivindicó marcando en el triunfo del Lille ante el Toyes tras ser expulsado contra el Betis en Champions
articles.body: La todavía precoz carrera de Ethan Mbappé (Montreuil, 2006) siempre ha estado ligada a la de su hermano Kylian... así como la de Davide Ancelotti a la de su padre Carlo. Ambos convergen ahora en las filas de un Lille que marcha líder de la Ligue 1 y se están ayudando el uno al otro para comenzar a escribir su propio camino. Dentro de esta relación que están forjando, les ha tocado vivir una semana realmente intensa. Ethan, titular durante los tres primeros partidos de la temporada, volvió a partir de inicio en el estreno de la Champions frente al Betis... y repartió la asistencia del 1-0 en favor de Ueda. Los de Pellegrini, sin embargo, lograron darle la vuelta al partido y, ‘víctima’ de unas provocaciones por parte de Natan, condenó al Lille siendo expulsado antes de llegar a la hora de encuentro tras propiciarle un ‘codazo’ al brasileño. “En el fútbol hay mucha frustración. Hay que gestionar las emociones. Y eso es algo que el equipo ha pagado hoy, que ha pagado Ethan, y que alguien más puede pagar mañana”, dijo Davide en rueda de prensa tras el choque. “Nos va a servir para gestionar la frustración. Mi discurso iba dirigido a todos los jugadores, no solo a Ethan. Por supuesto, va a aprender de esto porque es un jugador joven. Creo que es el primero que está arrepentido, que sabe que no puede hacer eso”. De alguna manera, trató de quitarle hierro al asunto. Pero, quizás a modo de ‘castigo’ para que terminase de tomar conciencia, Davide dejó a Ethan en el banquillo por primera vez esta temporada contra el Troyes. Salió en la segunda parte y, ya en el tiempo de descuento, se encargó de confirmar el triunfo marcando su primer gol de la temporada a pase de Kjaergaard con una sutil definición de primeras por debajo de las piernas de Patrick Beach. Días, atrás, en sus redes sociales, había pedido perdón por lo sucedido ante el Betis. “La derrota es culpa mía y asumo la responsabilidad”. L’Équipe, incluso, cuenta que Ethan se dirigió al despacho de Davide y le regaló una botella de Borgoña en señal de disculpa. “Los jugadores que hacen eso saben que los estaré esperando en los días siguientes”. Ya para finalizar, en el momento de la celebración de su gol contra el Troyes, lo primero que hizo Ethan fue dirigirse hacia el banderín de córner y pedir disculpas ante el Pierre Mauroy. Ya en un tono más reflexivo, Davide trató de extraer la parte positiva de todo lo sucedido durante estos últimos días alrededor de Ethan Mbappé. “Puedo decir que fue una semana muy importante para su crecimiento personal y como jugador. Se dio cuenta de lo que había hecho de inmediato y demostró una gran madurez para su edad. Asumió la responsabilidad enseguida. Por mi parte, no tuve mucho que hacer”. Davide, incluso, apuntó que guarda “una relación de hermano mayor” con un Ethan Mbappé que sólo quiere dejar este episodio atrás, pasar página y seguir creciendo en las filas de un Lille donde tiene como objetivo consolidarse en banda derecha. Es, de hecho, el jugador del equipo que más ocasiones claras ha creados (2) y el segundo que más pases clave promedia (1.5) por partido. Sabe que no es Kylian. Pero quiere escribir su propia historia... y esto forma parte del camino. La semana acabó por todo lo alto para Ethan Mbappé. Sin haber disputado ningún partido con las inferiores de Francia, recibió la convocatoria de la Sub21 para seguir preparando la clasificación al Europeo que tendrá lugar el próximo verano. Jugarán ante Islandia, Estonia, Luxemburgo y Suiza. De momento, marchan líderes e invictos en su grupo de clasificación. "Hay jugadores que se unen al grupo porque han rendido bien con sus clubes y han demostrado un gran potencial", expuso el seleccionador, Gérald Baticle. A pesar de poder representar a Argelia y Camerún, que ya mantuvieron algún contacto para tantear la situación, el sueño de Ethan sigue siendo jugar con su hermano en Francia. Ahora, a sus 19 años, ya ha dado ese primer paso.

articles.title: Manuel Ángel pide paso en el Fulham de su valedor Arbeloa: “Debo jugar con más intensidad y compromiso que nunca”
articles.standfirst: Disputó poco menos de media hora en su debut contra el West Ham y registró un 95.5% de acierto en el pase (28/29)
articles.summary: Disputó poco menos de media hora en su debut contra el West Ham y registró un 95.5% de acierto en el pase (28/29)
articles.body: El ‘spanish’ Fulham, poco a poco, comienza a coger oxígeno gracias, en parte, al impulso de La Fábrica que ha montado Álvaro Arbeloa en Craven Cottage: César Palacios, Gonzalo García y, también, un Manuel Ángel (Sevilla, 2004) que no ha tardado en pedir mando en plaza en la medular tras hacer su debut en la victoria contra el West Ham correspondiente a la tercera ronda de la Carabao Cup. Arbeloa siempre ha sido el gran valedor de ‘Mami’. Fue su capitán por las categorías inferiores del Real Madrid y le hizo debutar con el primer equipo la temporada pasada. Algunos veían su físico (1.70 m) como una gran limitación. Álvaro, sin embargo, nunca dudó de su potencial. “Yo he tenido mucha suerte en mi carrera de jugar con jugadores maravillosos. Hemos sido campeones del mundo y de Europa con gente que no pasaba del 1,70 y nadie se preocupaba”, reivindicaba. El propio Arbeloa, con quien Manuel Ángel acabó disputando seis encuentros con el Real Madrid el curso pasado, insistió en que “no iba a tener problemas para ser un jugador de élite” y lo definió como uno de sus “ojitos derechos”. No lo terminaron de ver así en la ‘Casa Blanca’ y, tras un verano repleto de incertidumbres alrededor de su futuro, se lo llevó para Londres. “Es una sensación increíble haber firmado por un club tan legendario como el Fulham, el club más antiguo de Londres. También es una sensación increíble competir en la Premier League, un lugar donde todo jugador sueña con jugar en algún momento de su carrera”, dijo en su presentación un Manuel Ángel que, lógicamente, agradeció la confianza depositada por Arbeloa. “Es un verdadero privilegio. Le conozco desde hace muchos años y es un entrenador que saca lo mejor de los jugadores”. Manuel Ángel, consciente del salto que suponía pasar de competir regularmente en Primera RFEF a hacerlo en la Premier League, apuntaba que debía jugar “con más intensidad y compromiso que nunca”. Sin minutos en la dolorosa derrota contra el Crystal Palace y el valioso punto —el primero de la temporada — obtenido en Anfield, Arbeloa le dio la oportunidad de debutar en el London Stadium ante el West Ham en Carabao Cup. Saltó al césped con empate (2-2) en el marcador y poco menos de media hora por delante en sustitución de Hugo Larsson. Desde el principio, sin embargo, mostró una personalidad arrolladora para pedir la pelota y organizar los ataques de un Fulham que acabaría llevándose el partido (2-3) para avanzar a la siguiente ronda. Apoyándose en su centro de gravedad bajo para girar y escaneo constante de la situación antes de recibir, dejó claro que es un centrocampista tremendamente mandón. De hecho, apenas erró uno de los 29 pases que intentó. “Tenemos muchos jugadores jóvenes con talento y necesitamos ser pacientes con ellos. Hay que ayudarles y desarrollarlos, pero se ve el talento y la calidad que tienen. Entienden el juego y crecerán a lo largo de la temporada”, auguraba Arbeloa, también en alusión a Manuel Ángel, después del encuentro. Sabe que no lo tendrá fácil para ‘colarse’ en una medular donde campan Berge, Iwobi, Shea Charles o Hugo Larsson. Pero, por si acaso, ya va pidiendo sitio.

articles.title: Brighton & Hove Albion news: Albion celebrate 125th anniversary
articles.summary: From obscurity and near oblivion to Premier League and Europe - Brighton celebrate their 125th anniversary.
articles.body:
It is Thursday, 9 November, 2023. Brighton manager Roberto de Zerbi is addressing his players in the Amsterdam Arena before their Europa League tie with Ajax.

"There's 3,000 Brighton fans in this stadium tonight," said the Italian. "But there's more than twice that number in the city who have travelled over. Remember that when you go on to that pitch."

A long-standing senior Brighton official was in the dressing room that day. A fan first and foremost, but someone who has spent almost three decades working for the club.

"It made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up," he said.

For some clubs, an encounter with Ajax is commonplace. Not Brighton .

"The royalty of European football," says the official. "From where we've come from, to be in that environment. It was a pinch-me moment."

Brighton won 2-0. It was the high point of the first European campaign in the club's history.

Ask Paul Samrah for his single most memorable moment as a Brighton fan and a very different answer comes back, which goes to the heart of why, as they celebrate their 125th birthday around the visit of Arsenal , the Seagulls are almost unique among English clubs.

August 2007. "After the years of campaigning, the days and nights I spent fighting for regime change and then for the stadium, the moment I heard we'd actually got planning permission, that our objectors had decided not to continue their fruitless efforts to stop the stadium," he explained.

The two stories highlight the before and after reality of Brighton & Hove Albion .

Formed in 1901, Brighton were a Southern League club for almost two decades before they were voted into the Football League. They had experienced only seven seasons in Division Two when they were promoted to the top flight for the first time in 1979.

For years, they were known outside Sussex chiefly for "And Smith must score..." - the BBC radio commentary, delivered by the late Peter Jones, at a critical point during the 1983 FA Cup final, late in extra time. It was the moment when Gordon Smith, clear on goal with a chance to earn Brighton their first major trophy, saw his shot saved by Manchester United goalkeeper Gary Bailey. United won the replay.

But in 1995, chairman Bill Archer sold Brighton 's Goldstone Ground, their home since 1902, because of escalating debts that there was no obvious way of paying. Fans were not consulted and no alternative stadium was put in place.

Brighton did not leave until 1997, although their final season at the Goldstone was only confirmed by the property company who owned the stadium, after the final game of the 1995-96 campaign, which had to be abandoned as thousands of furious fans spilled on to the pitch to demonstrate against the ownership. Both crossbars were snapped amid the tumult.

After two seasons playing 70 miles away at Gillingham, and with the idea of a new stadium in the Toad's Hole Valley area of Brighton a non-starter, the club returned to the city in 1999 and started playing at Withdean Stadium, most famous for being the home athletics track of Olympic middle distance gold medallist Steve Ovett.

That brings us back to De Zerbi's pre-match team-talk at Ajax.

Brighton had more than 7,000 fans in Amsterdam that night. When they moved into the Withdean, its capacity was only 6,000. The modern Brighton really is a totally different club to the one that existed before.

"After the 1983 FA Cup final, players were sold, there was no investment, the Goldstone was decaying and the crowds were dipping," said Samrah. "There was no communication between board and fans, directors came and went. There was no continuity, no leadership, no direction. We were just rudderless."

There are some notable figures in the Brighton story.

Former Football Association executive director David Davies got involved, Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott overturned a rejected planning application for Brighton 's current stadium in Falmer. Former chairman Dick Knight stabilised a club that in 1997 came within 27 minutes of being relegated out of the Football League.

Without that trio, and many more, it is quite possible Brighton would not exist.

The contemporary Brighton are different.

They began their second European campaign in the Norwegian city of Tromso last month, knowing the Conference League offers the chance of that elusive first trophy.

They play in a magnificent stadium, a short train journey from the city centre, with its new corporate areas, and, generally, inclusive family atmosphere. Their recruitment model, buying players in and selling them on for vast profits, is envied. The new Brighton just beat Manchester United at Old Trafford for the fifth time in six visits. Four games into their 10th consecutive Premier League campaign, they sit fifth.

The contemporary Brighton exist the way they do largely because of the vision and investment of Tony Bloom.

Born in Brighton , Bloom is a lifelong fan. His connection to the club is through his grandfather Harry, a former vice-chairman, and uncle Ray, a director.

Bloom, 56, is an entrepreneur. He made his money in finance and gambling, largely through the use of data. He became chairman in 2009, and masterminded the rise from League One and move into the American Express Stadium. Last season, Brighton 's average attendance was more than 31,000.

In their 125-year history, Brighton have never had it so good.

"Anyone walking into Brighton today compared to even 15 years ago would not think it was the same football club," sporting director Mike Cave told BBC Sport.

"The club has been on an unbelievable journey. We've got staff members and many fans who have done that journey. For those of us who weren't here 15 years ago, our responsibility is to ensure what's to come - and I think there's lots - is better than what's happened in the recent or long-distance past."

As for Bloom himself, he has reflected on Brighton 's 125th birthday in the programme for the Arsenal game.

"Since 1901, this football club has been part of the fabric of our city and the broader county of Sussex," he said.

"It has connected generations of families and communities. Grandparents have brought their children and grandchildren to matches. Lifelong friendships have been forged on terraces, in stands and on away trips.

"Through good times and bad, Brighton & Hove Albion has provided so many of us with some of the most memorable moments of our lives.

"This club is in my blood. Some of my earliest and most cherished memories are wrapped up in the sights and sounds of the Goldstone.

"When I had the privilege of becoming owner and chairman, it was like being entrusted with something precious to safeguard and help develop for the future.

"Many of you reading these words will remember those difficult years. The loss of the Goldstone. The long journeys to Gillingham. The challenges of the Withdean era.

"What got this football club through was the determination of its fans. The bucket collections. The protests. The refusal to accept the Albion should disappear. This anniversary belongs as much to those supporters as anyone. Quite simply, without them, we would not be here today."

Whether they beat Arsenal or not, Brighton stands tall, for those who fought to preserve something they felt was special, and a man who had a vision - and finance - to build something better.

articles.title: Dan Lanning Joins Oregon Legends with Elite Statistic
articles.summary: Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning has joined an elite list after the win over the Portland State Vikings.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks had a dominant 84-0 win over the Portland State Vikings on Friday night, which was a much-needed victory after a stunning loss to the Oklahoma State Cowboys in Week 2.

With the win over the Vikings, head coach Dan Lanning has etched his name in Oregon's history books, becoming the fourth coach in program history to win 50 games , joining Mike Bellotti, Rich Brooks, and Len Casanova.

Lanning has reached 50 wins in just his fifth season with the team and will look to continue picking up wins and move up the list throughout the year.

If he can help the Ducks turn around the season in 2026 and have at least a few more good seasons, he could cement himself as one of the best coaches in program history .

Oregon dropped in the AP Poll rankings after their loss to Oklahoma State and will need to build their way back up to have a shot at making the College Football Playoff.

The Ducks still possess a very talented roster led by stars like quarterback Dante Moore , but they will need consistent execution on both sides of the ball.

Moore had an exceptional game, completing 19 of 23 passes for 280 yards, four touchdowns, and zero interceptions. He didn't even play in the second half due to the 49-0 halftime lead.

Oregon had the execution they had been lacking in their win over Portland State , with 43 first downs compared to five for the Vikings. The Ducks also dominated in total yards, 723 to 103, and had zero turnovers compared to Portland State's four.

Oregon knew this was a must-win game and that they needed to dominate to prove they could be a competitive team. Oregon will need to use this momentum in their Week 4 matchup against the USC Trojans, who have emerged as one of the best teams in the Big Ten.

Lanning has proven to be a great coach for the Ducks over the last few years, but with a challenging start to the season, he has a tall task ahead to get his team ready to take on a strong Trojans team.

articles.title: Belgium coach explains chat with Real Madrid veteran after Nations League exclusion: ‘If anything happens…’
articles.summary: Thibaut Courtois will not be part of Mark van Bommel’s first Belgium squad, with the Real Madrid goalkeeper sitting out the upcoming Nations League fixtures...
articles.body:
Thibaut Courtois will not be part of Mark van Bommel's first Belgium squad, with the Real Madrid goalkeeper sitting out the upcoming Nations League fixtures after reaching an agreement with the new national team coach.

Courtois had already made clear that he intended to step away from Belgium's Nations League campaign, prioritising his workload and recovery after a demanding period with Real Madrid.

Van Bommel subsequently travelled to Madrid to discuss the situation directly with the 34-year-old.

The meeting ended with both sides agreeing that Courtois would remain out of the squad for the upcoming fixtures, although Van Bommel has not closed the door on a return.

Van Bommel leaves door open for Courtois

Speaking during the squad announcement (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), Van Bommel explained that the decision followed his conversation with Courtois and stressed that they would remain in contact.

Courtois has not been included in Belgium's squad for the Nations League. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

"I went to Madrid. We spoke and came to the conclusion that he would sit out the Nations League."

The Belgium coach also acknowledged that circumstances could change, particularly if the squad suffers injuries, while stopping short of promising Courtois a place later in the competition.

"And if anything happens between now and then, we'll stay in touch. We'll see how the situation develops, although I can't guarantee he will play."

Van Bommel was nevertheless unequivocal about Courtois' standing as a goalkeeper. Despite the decision to leave him out, the new coach still regards the Real Madrid star among the elite in world football.

"We don't know how far we'll get in the Nations League. I think you've seen him play too. Thibaut is still among the best in the world," he concluded.

Courtois chooses recovery during international breaks

Courtois voluntarily decided not to play the Nations League matches. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Courtois had previously explained his position when he confirmed that he would not participate in Belgium's Nations League fixtures, including the Final Four, unless the national team faced an exceptional injury crisis.

"I'm not going to play any Nations League matches, not even the Final Four, unless the coach needs me because there are too many injuries," he noted.

The decision is part of a change in how the veteran goalkeeper is managing his international commitments.

After years of representing Belgium, Courtois now wants to use international windows to recover, train and reduce the physical demands placed on him.

As a result, the decision gives him an opportunity to use the international break away from competitive matches and prepare for the remainder of the club season.

articles.summary: College Football fans are eagerly anticipating one of the most highly anticipated games in recent SEC history. Lane Kiffin is set to make his return to Ole M...
articles.body:
College Football fans are eagerly anticipating one of the most highly anticipated games in recent SEC history. Lane Kiffin is set to make his return to Ole Miss as he brings LSU into Vaught-Hemingway Stadium to take on the Rebels.

Both teams enter the matchup with spotless 2-0 records, and now the long-awaited Week 3 showdown has arrived. Before the highly anticipated game, Ole Miss legend Eli Manning grabbed the fans' attention after starring in a hype video released by the program.

CFB Fans Not Sold on Eli Manning's Narration of Ole Miss Hype Video

The Rebels have a long-standing tradition of producing elite quarterbacks, and Eli Manning undoubtedly remains one of the most recognizable names in the program's history.

Ahead of the exciting LSU vs. Ole Miss showdown, the program shared a video on X, with Manning providing the dramatic narration.

"This game needs no introduction," Manning said in the video. "Generations of bad blood tell the story. It flowed through the river for over a century, fueled with passion, and guaranteed to give you goosebumps.

"This moment is what we prepare for on Saturday night; the center of the college football world is in Oxford, Mississippi. It's Ole Miss versus LSU."

Manning's dramatic, goosebumps-inducing narration quickly put the Ole Miss legend in the spotlight, but fans didn't hesitate to flood the comments section with jokes and criticism directed at the NFL legend.

"Maybe they can do something Eli couldn't," a fan reacted .

"With this weak of a hype video, LSU's about to smoke 'em by 50," one comment read .

"I mean y'all could have picked a player to narrate who actually had a win versus LSU," one user joked .

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

"I'm not gonna lie, this did not hype me up one bit lol," a fan joked .

"Carve your name into history one more time? Remind me what you've done that is historic. Is it your 0 appearances in the SEC title game? One measly national championship that nobody can confirm is legit? What exactly have you done?" a user remarked .

Manning finished his illustrious Ole Miss career with a then-school-record 10,119 career passing yards and 81 career touchdown passes. He also established Ole Miss career records for completions and passing attempts, with both figures ranking fourth on the SEC's career lists.

During his Ole Miss career, Manning won the Maxwell Award and Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award while also earning several All-America honors.

Despite his impressive accomplishments at Ole Miss, the Rebels legend was unable to establish a dominant record against LSU during his college career. Manning finished 1-2 in three career games against the Tigers.

However, for now, CFB fans are focused on the upcoming LSU vs. Ole Miss showdown because of Kiffin's return to Oxford.

Kiffin guided Ole Miss to an 11-1 record in 2025 before leaving the program for LSU just before the College Football Playoff.

articles.title: Here we go: Barcelona complete signing of 16-year-old attacking midfielder
articles.summary: Barcelona have completed the signing of 16-year-old attacking talent Dany Freire, with Fabrizio Romano giving his trademark ‘Here We Go’ to the move.The Port...
articles.body:
Barcelona have completed the signing of 16-year-old attacking talent Dany Freire, with Fabrizio Romano giving his trademark 'Here We Go' to the move.

The Portuguese-Luxembourgish youngster passed his trial with Barcelona and is signing his contract with the club today, with the remaining formalities now set to be completed.

Born in Lisbon on 19 September 2010, Freire moved to Luxembourg at a young age and developed his football at Racing FC Union Letzebuerg.

He holds both Portuguese and Luxembourgish nationality and has represented Portugal at youth level after previously featuring for Luxembourg.

Barcelona move for versatile attacking talent

As such, Freire's versatility was one of the qualities that caught Barcelona's attention .

Dany Freire has signed for Barcelona. (Picture credit: Instagram/@dany_freire9)

He can operate as an attacking midfielder, on the left wing or through the middle as a centre-forward, giving him several routes into the attacking positions.

Barcelona had already identified the teenager during his time with Racing Union, where he impressed in Luxembourg's youth competitions.

His performances in the UEFA Youth League and domestic cup football helped put him on the club's radar before he was invited to join Barcelona's summer training camps.

Furthermore, his trial period with the Juvenil B side then strengthened the club's interest. Freire scored on his debut in a pre-season friendly against CF Badalona and continued to attract attention during the summer tournaments.

Freire impressed Barcelona after trial spell

The teenager scored three goals during the summer competitions, collected an MVP award and was part of the Barcelona side that defeated Real Madrid in a youth Clasico.

Dany Freire impressed Barcelona with his versatility. (Picture credit: Instagram/@dany_freire9)

Those displays convinced the coaching staff working under Juvenil B coach Cesc Bosch that Freire was worth pursuing on a permanent basis.

The timing of the agreement was also dictated by FIFA regulations. As a non-Spanish player, Freire could not formally sign for Barcelona before turning 16.

That restriction has now been removed with his birthday, allowing Barcelona to complete the administrative steps and formalise the agreement.

Freire is expected to begin his Barcelona career with Juvenil B, where he will continue his development after making a strong impression during his trial.

articles.title: INTERVIEW: "I needed to play a bigger role" – Cole Campbell on leaving Dortmund for Elversberg
articles.summary: Four years after joining Borussia Dortmund from Icelandic side Breiðablik, Cole Campbell decided it was time to move on this summer, joining newly-promoted B...
articles.body:
Four years after joining Borussia Dortmund from Icelandic side Breiðablik, Cole Campbell decided it was time to move on this summer, joining newly-promoted Bundesliga side SV Elversberg, who paid a club-record €6 million fee to sign him.

Campbell's future with the Black and Yellows looked bright when he made his senior debut at just 18 in October 2024. Ultimately, though, his career at Dortmund never quite took off, and the now 20-year-old decided it was time for a change after making just five appearances for TSG Hoffenheim during an injury-hit loan spell in the second half of last season.

"The main thing was that I needed to get minutes for my career, to play a lot more and have a bigger role than I had at Dortmund," Campbell said when Bulinews.com asked him about his decision to join SV Elversberg this summer during a media roundtable.

So far, Campbell has gotten the playing time he was looking for, starting all four of Elversberg's games this season. His performances have also earned him his first call-up to the senior U.S. national team.

"The move was very important for me, and now I'm getting minutes, which is the most important thing for me to develop and become the best player I can be. I think the step in my career was the right one, and I'm happy that I came here," said the 20-year-old, who finally scored his first Bundesliga goal in Elversberg's opening 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen , two years after making his league debut for Borussia Dortmund.

"To score my first goal was an amazing feeling. It was very important for the team, and for us to win the game was amazing. It was the first game we had in the Bundesliga, so to start off with a win was amazing. It was very important for us and myself, and I'm really happy about it," Campbell said.

Asked about his difficult spell of nearly two years without regular playing time, Campbell took a positive approach, saying the challenging period has strengthened both his faith and his mental toughness.

"The expectation from last season was to play more than what I did. But I'm a strong believer in Jesus, and I believe that God has a plan. I believe this time strengthened my relationship with Him and my mental toughness," he said.

Although the frustration was difficult to deal with in the moment, Campbell held on to his faith and believes the experience ultimately helped him grow both as a person and a player.

"Things can change in six months, and I'm always trusting in the plan God has for me and not being afraid of missing it or anything like that. I think even in this time, where someone else would look at it and say it was a waste, it was something that I learned and something I could take from it. I'm thankful for this time.

"I wouldn't have learned the things I did in these 22 months if things had happened differently. My relationship with God has gotten stronger in these two years, and my mindset has changed. I can speak about the frustration in the moment, but without this, my character wouldn't change.

"Everything happened the way it was supposed to, and I'm thankful for the time and for the things I've learned along the way."

In the footsteps of Woltemade and Asllani

Elversberg have become known as a club willing to give young players opportunities, with the likes of Nick Woltemade, Fisnik Asllani and Paul Wanner all taking significant development steps at the club in recent years. That naturally strengthened Elversberg's case when Campbell was considering his next move.

"Of course they told me about this, and I also looked into it myself. Whenever you want to join a club, it's important that you learn what they've done in the past, which obviously influences how you feel about going there. I had a lot of conversations with the coach, the sporting director and the people around the club. They explained their plan and what the club is about," Campbell said.

"When you have other players who have gone there, gotten their minutes, developed and made a big step for themselves, it obviously helps. It had an influence on me coming here. In the end, I think it was the right step. I decided I needed to get more minutes and have a club that believes in me, that gives me the support and the backing to become the best version of myself. In the end, I'm happy that I came here."

Being Elversberg's record signing naturally comes with a certain amount of pressure, but Campbell also feels the necessary trust and support from everyone at the club.

"Obviously there's pressure that comes with it, but on the other side, there's also a lot of trust from them to believe in me and have trust in me. Since I've come here, I've felt very good. Everyone at the club is supporting each other. The pressure I put on myself to perform was already there before the money was involved," Campbell stressed, adding:

"Regardless of these things, I want to perform every game and do my best. That's what I'll continue doing, trying to become better in every game and training session. I think there's pressure there, but the support I have from the club, my teammates and the coaching staff is also there, which helps me have a good feeling to perform."

Campbell will have his next chance to find the net when Elversberg face fellow newly-promoted side Schalke 04 at the Veltins-Arena on Sunday at 17:30 CEST, before linking up with the US national team for the upcoming international break.
